messages:
Alice M.: Heads-up: ran a quick perf sweep on the FlashAttention v2/v3 selector heuristics against the small/medium/long seq buckets. Some odd regressions for short sequences when KV cache is hot.
Ben K.: hmm, short seq regressions? can you paste the numbers?
Alice M.: Summary: v3 wins on long sequences (>1024) by ~22% p99 latency, v2 slightly better on medium (256-512), but on short (<64) v3 is ~8% slower at median when KV cache hit rate >80%.
Carla S.: that's surprising — v3 was supposed to be universally better. Might be a scheduling or kernel launch overhead for tiny tokens.
Alice M.: I profiled kernel-level times, looks like extra memcpy + kernel setup when paged-KV path is taken. snippet:```
# kernel timings (ms)
seq=16, kv_hit=95%: v2_total=1.6 v3_total=1.7
seq=512, kv_hit=60%: v2_total=8.2 v3_total=6.3
seq=2048, kv_hit=40%: v2_total=28.1 v3_total=21.9
```
Ryan T.: can you share the perf traces? also which cuda kernels? flash_kern_v2 vs flash_kern_v3?
Alice M.: attached trace gist: https://rwd/g/trace/abc123 (mock link). Kernels: flash_attn_v2_kernel, flash_attn_v3_paged_kernel, and a new `kv_stitch` kernel that runs only on v3 when paged-KV enabled.
Monica L.: kv_stitch rings a bell — it does extra reordering for cache pages. That overhead could dominate for tiny seqs.
Ben K.: what's the current selector logic? cost_model + heuristic: if seq>1024 pick v3, else pick v2 unless kv_paged==true then pick v3.
Carla S.: That last clause (kv_paged -> v3) might be the problem. For short seqs, paged-KV has very cheap lookups but the kv_stitch kernel overhead wins.
Alice M.: Proposed change: add microcost estimate for kv_stitch in selector and a fast-path that picks v2 for seq<64 even if paged-KV is on. Also add feature flag `ff/attn_kernel_kv_microcost` to toggle.
Ryan T.: +1. Can we put the selector change behind a rolling flag initially? I want a canary on Dedicated pools first.
Monica L.: ops question: how will this interact with autop-runner batching? If we change selector, batching buckets might shift and affect throughput. Need AB test on per-route throughput and unit cost.
Ben K.: plan: 1) add microcost to selector + FF (ff/attn_kernel_kv_microcost). 2) Canary on dedicated-east-1 (small %), run 48h, compare p50/p95/p99 and token-cost. 3) If stable, ramp to 25% then 100%. 4) separate AB to see batching distribution delta.
Carla S.: I'll add unit tests for selector with mocked kernel costs and kv flags. Also add telemetry events: chosen_kernel, seq_len_bucket, kv_hit_rate, estimated_cost.
Alice M.: Telemetry schema draft: `attn.kernel_choice`, `attn.seq_bucket`, `attn.kv_mode`, `attn.estimated_kernel_ms`, `attn.observed_ms`. Will attach proto in PR.
Ryan T.: OpsBot: create rollout ticket for canary + dashboard.
OpsBot: Created ticket RWD-INT-2145 and dashboard rwd/dash/attn-kernel-canary (ETA: 2h).
Monica L.: Danger note: if the microcost estimate is stale across GPUs (A100 vs H100) we may misroute. Need device-aware kernel cost table per GPU family.
Ben K.: good catch — include device_family in selector key and cost table. Default fallback to conservative (pick v2) if unknown.
Alice M.: I'll prototype with A100/H100 entries. Bench script is `tools/bench/attn_kernel_scorecard.py` if you want to reproduce.
Carla S.: timing-wise: PR for selector + telemetry by EOD, FF wired in launch config, canary start earliest tomorrow 09:00 PT.
Ryan T.: I'll own the canary monitoring and rollback criteria (5% latency reg at p99 or 3% cost increase triggers rollback).
Ben K.: one more item: batching heuristics. If selector flips more short seqs to v2, backlog distribution in autobatcher may concentrate many small reqs -> decreased batching efficiency. Add a metric for average batch size per route.
Alice M.: noted. I'll add `attn.batch_size_avg` to telemetry and a short runbook for when avg batch size drops >15% vs baseline.
Monica L.: thanks all. Also leave FF default=false in prod until canary passes.
Alice M.: SG. I'll open the PR and ping this thread. :thumbsup:
Carla S.: thanks — signoff after tests pass.
Ben K.: sounds good.
Ryan T.: ready on my side for monitoring.
Alice M.: PR: https://rwd/p/pr/890 (will upload traces and bench outputs).
